title: Anthropic's filing, Gemini's clock
summary: Anthropic's IPO filing turns a model vendor into a disclosed counterparty, and marketing could start the week of November ninth. Also: Gemini 3.6 Flash retires on November nineteenth, the AI Act marking date is four weeks away, and agent gateways keep spreading while Walmart's Agent Profiles are still pending.
headlines: Anthropic's IPO filing puts vendor risk on the table
AI Act marking date is four weeks away

story_of_the_day.facts: CBS News reports that Anthropic has filed for an IPO. CNBC's coverage of the filing cites revenue retention of 900 percent and first-half losses of about 80 billion dollars. Digiday says the filing shows a fast-growing advertising bill. According to reports, marketing for the offering could begin the week of November ninth. None of this is final: the timing is reported, not announced by the company, and I have not seen the filing text itself. Separately, ActuIA's coverage of the Artificial Analysis index version five puts Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 and Claude Haiku 5.5 at 36.
story_of_the_day.read: The read here: a public filing turns a vendor into a counterparty you can analyse. For a platform team, the interesting parts are the ones a model card never shows: compute commitments, customer concentration, how revenue splits between API and subscriptions. That is useful input for vendor risk files. It does not change today's availability or pricing. What it likely does is sharpen two habits. Keep a second vendor warm behind your gateway for every critical route. And ask for price protection and long deprecation notice in contracts. Worth watching: the week of November ninth.
story_of_the_day.label: reported

segments.facts: Google's model lifecycle page for its enterprise agent platform lists gemini-3.6-flash as retiring on November nineteenth, with gemini-3.8-flash as the replacement. Help Net Security covered the launch of Gemini 3.8 Flash on September third.
segments.read: Why it matters: since that launch was covered in early September, you can test the replacement now, not in the final days before retirement. Search gateway logs for pinned 3.6 identifiers, and run your own evaluation set on 3.8 Flash. Compare cost per completed task, not list price. Give every pinned identifier an owner and an expiry date.
segments.label: confirmed

segments.facts: The European Commission says the AI Omnibus entered into force on July twenty-seventh, 2026. High-risk rules for Annex III systems now apply from December second, 2027. Rules for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products apply from August second, 2028. A Cloud Security Alliance note flags December second, 2026 as the end of the grace period for marking AI-generated content.
segments.read: The bigger picture: high-risk got a year of breathing room, marking did not. December second is twenty-nine days away. For a retailer, generated product text, images and chat answers are the first places to look. Build the inventory of generative features now, and name one owner for marking. Check the exact scope with legal.
segments.label: confirmed

segments.facts: Insurify published a release announcing an AI Agent Gateway built around the Model Context Protocol, WebMCP and what it calls agent pathways. Walmart said on October twenty-first that its Agent Profiles would launch within a month. I found no launch notice by this morning.
segments.read: What this really signals: the front door for agents is becoming a product, from retail to insurance. The pattern is the same. Identify the agent, expose structured actions, set limits. For a retailer, the question is less which protocol wins and more whether product data and stock APIs are clean enough to expose. Likely, but unproven, that standards converge.
segments.label: confirmed

number_of_the_day.text: November nineteenth. That is the retirement date for Gemini 3.6 Flash, according to Google's lifecycle page. Any pinned route still on it needs a tested replacement before then.
